paragraphs.context: At this school, you will be learning side by side with dragons
paragraphs.mainIdea: A school for all the tribes.
paragraphs.simple: This page is a welcome letter from Jade Mountain Academy. Young dragons from all the tribes study there together, so the next pages give some facts about each tribe.

paragraphs.context: You have been assigned to a winglet with six other dragons;
paragraphs.mainIdea: Each student is in a winglet.
paragraphs.simple: Every student is put in a small class called a winglet, with six dragons from other tribes. The list of winglets comes on the next page.

background.note: At Jade Mountain Academy, a small class of seven dragonets, one from each tribe.

paragraphs.context: WE WISH YOU ALL THE POWER OF WINGS OF FIRE!
paragraphs.simple: The letter says the students are the hope for a long peace in Pyrrhia. It ends with a wish. "Wings of fire" is a phrase from the old Dragonet Prophecy; here it means "may you be strong and do great things".

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can survive a long time without water, poison enemies with the tips
paragraphs.simple: SandWings can live a long time without water. They can poison enemies with the end of their tail, like a scorpion, hide under the sand, and breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: since the end of the War of SandWing Succession, Queen Thorn
paragraphs.mainIdea: The SandWings have a new queen.
paragraphs.simple: There was a long war about who would be the SandWing queen. That war is over now, and Thorn is the queen.

background.note: The war that began when Queen Oasis died and her three daughters fought to be queen of the SandWings. Most of the tribes joined in.
Thorn is now queen of the SandWings.

paragraphs.context: Students at Jade Mountain: Arid, Onyx, Ostrich, Pronghorn, Qibli
paragraphs.simple: These are the five SandWing students at the school. Each tribe page ends with a list like this.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire (if warm enough), hold their breath for up
paragraphs.simple: MudWings can breathe fire when they are warm, stay under water or mud for an hour without breathing, and hide in mud. They are very strong.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: powerful fighters and fliers, can breathe fire
paragraphs.simple: SkyWings are strong fighters and fast fliers, and they can breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Queen Ruby (although some dragons still support Queen Scarlet,
paragraphs.simple: Ruby is the SkyWing queen now. But some SkyWings still want Scarlet, the old queen who lost her throne. Scarlet may still be alive and hiding somewhere.

background.note: Ruby is Queen Scarlet's daughter. After Scarlet loses her throne, Ruby becomes queen of the SkyWings.
Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.

paragraphs.context: Description: blue or green or aquamarine scales; webs between their claws; gills
paragraphs.simple: SeaWings are blue or green. They have skin between their claws, gills for breathing under water, and stripes that glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can withstand subzero temperatures and bright light, exhale a deadly frostbreath
paragraphs.simple: IceWings can live in very cold places and in bright light, and they breathe out frostbreath, a deadly freezing breath.

background.note: The deadly freezing breath of IceWings; it can freeze and kill other dragons.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can camouflage their scales to blend into their surroundings;
paragraphs.simple: RainWings can change the colors of their scales to hide and match the things around them. They can also shoot deadly venom (poison) from their fangs.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire, disappear into dark shadows; once known for reading minds
paragraphs.simple: NightWings can breathe fire and hide in dark shadows. Long ago they were famous for reading minds and seeing the future, but the guide says they cannot do this anymore.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Queen Glory (see recent scrolls on the NightWing Exodus and
paragraphs.simple: Glory, the RainWing queen, is now the queen of the NightWings too. The page says you can read about how this happened in new scrolls: the NightWings left their old home (the Exodus), and there was a contest for the RainWing throne.

background.note: Glory is a RainWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is the queen of the RainWings, and now of the NightWings too.
The time when the NightWings left their island home.
The contest for the RainWing throne.

paragraphs.context: Beware the darkness of dragons,
paragraphs.simple: This is the Jade Mountain Prophecy, a new message about the future. It starts with warnings. "Beware" means "be careful of". "The darkness of dragons" means dragons who are evil or dangerous. "The stalker of dreams" is someone who follows dragons secretly, even in their dreams.

paragraphs.context: Beware the talons of power and fire,
paragraphs.simple: "Talons" are a dragon's claws. "The talons of power and fire" means a strong, dangerous dragon. The next line warns about a female dragon who is not what she seems: she hides who she really is.

paragraphs.context: Something is coming to shake the earth,
paragraphs.simple: Something terrible is coming. It will shake the ground and burn it. The prophecy does not say what it is.

paragraphs.context: Jade Mountain will fall beneath thunder and ice
paragraphs.simple: Here "fall" means "be destroyed". Jade Mountain, where the school is, will be destroyed by thunder and ice, unless dragons can find "the lost city of night". The prophecy does not say what the thunder and ice are, or where that city is.

background.note: A tall mountain in the middle of Pyrrhia with many caves inside it.

paragraphs.context: No dragon was safe in the Sky Palace, but the
paragraphs.simple: No dragon is safe in Queen Scarlet's palace, and her daughters are in the most danger of all.

background.note: The palace of the SkyWing queen, high in the mountains.
Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.

paragraphs.context: Ruby hadn’t seen her sister, Tourmaline, in three days.
paragraphs.simple: Ruby has not seen her sister Tourmaline for three days.

background.note: Ruby is Queen Scarlet's daughter. After Scarlet loses her throne, Ruby becomes queen of the SkyWings.
Tourmaline is a SkyWing princess, Ruby's sister.

paragraphs.context: Not since the night they went flying together and, high
paragraphs.simple: The last time they flew together, Tourmaline whispered that she was almost ready to challenge their mother.

paragraphs.context: “Don’t be an idiot. You’re only ten, and furthermore, you’ll
paragraphs.simple: Ruby tells her she is too young. Scarlet killed her own mother, her sisters and eleven of her daughters.

paragraphs.context: “Twenty-four years is a long time but not that long,”
paragraphs.simple: Tourmaline says Scarlet has ruled for twenty-four years, but even Queen Oasis did not rule forever.

background.note: Queen Oasis was the SandWing queen before the war. After she died, her three daughters fought over her throne.

paragraphs.context: “Are you planning to throw a scavenger at Mother?” Ruby
paragraphs.simple: Ruby asks if Tourmaline plans to throw a scavenger at their mother, because Scarlet would just eat it before she killed her.

background.note: Dragons call humans 'scavengers'. In these books scavengers are small, clever people whom dragons often see as pests or pets.

paragraphs.context: “It’s always going to be like this,” Tourmaline hissed. She
paragraphs.simple: Tourmaline says she and Ruby are the last sisters left. If she becomes queen, the SkyWings can leave the war.

background.note: Red and orange dragons with huge wings who live in the mountains of the Sky Kingdom. They are strong fighters and fast fliers.

paragraphs.context: Ruby wasn’t so sure about that. She’d met Burn, and
paragraphs.simple: Ruby has met Burn, the SandWing ally, and doubts she would let the SkyWings leave the war.

background.note: Burn was one of three SandWing sisters who fought to be queen. She was huge and violent.
The desert dragons of Pyrrhia. They have pale gold scales and a poisonous barb on the end of the tail, and they can live a long time without water.

paragraphs.context: “The prophecy will take care of the war,” she argued.
paragraphs.simple: Ruby says the prophecy will end the war. The brightest night is only four days away.

background.note: A message that tells what will happen in the future. NightWings who can see the future give prophecies.
A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: “Right.” Tourmaline rolled her eyes. “I’ll just wait for a
paragraphs.simple: Tourmaline does not want to wait for eggs to save them. She wants to act.

paragraphs.context: She’s wondering if I want the throne for myself, Ruby
paragraphs.simple: Ruby sees that Tourmaline wonders if Ruby secretly wants the throne too.

paragraphs.context: “Well, don’t worry, I won’t do it yet,” Tourmaline promised.
paragraphs.simple: Tourmaline promises to wait a few more months. She says she beat their brother Vermilion in a fight.

background.note: Vermilion is a SkyWing prince, one of Queen Scarlet's sons.

paragraphs.context: But then she was gone. And the most unsettling thing
paragraphs.simple: Then Tourmaline is gone, and nobody even mentions it. No one is searching for her.

paragraphs.context: There were no splatters of blood. No sign of a
paragraphs.simple: There is no blood and no note in their room.

paragraphs.context: Did Tourmaline change her mind and run away? Could she
paragraphs.simple: Ruby wonders if Tourmaline ran away to the Talons of Peace.

background.note: A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: But Ruby knew that wasn’t what had happened. Her big
paragraphs.simple: But Tourmaline was not the kind to run away, and Scarlet would never let her daughter join the peace movement.

paragraphs.context: Never let them see that you’re terrified, that’s what Tourmaline
paragraphs.simple: Tourmaline always said never to show fear. But maybe acting like a queen is what got her killed.

paragraphs.context: “Thank you,” Ruby said, inclining her head at the guard
paragraphs.simple: Ruby is only five years old. Her heart pounds as she walks to the throne room.

background.note: A young dragon, not yet fully grown.

paragraphs.context: Dragons huddled by the throne room entrance, whispering; they all
paragraphs.simple: Dragons outside the throne room wonder, like Ruby, if Scarlet is getting rid of daughters who might threaten her.

paragraphs.context: Ruby ducked her long neck as she entered the room
paragraphs.simple: The room is hot, bright with gold and full of courtiers.

paragraphs.context: “Ah, Ruby.” The queen’s voice lilted over all the others
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet tells the court that Ruby is quiet and bookish, nothing like her mother.

paragraphs.context: “Well, now everyone is here! Everyone important, I mean. I
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet says she has exciting news and tells Ruby to stand with her brothers.

paragraphs.context: The crowd parted to let Ruby through, their avid orange
paragraphs.simple: Ruby stands between Vermilion and Hawk. All of Scarlet's children are there except Tourmaline.

background.note: Hawk is a SkyWing prince, one of Queen Scarlet's sons.

paragraphs.context: Vermilion snorted and edged a step away from her, but
paragraphs.mainIdea: Hawk is nice for a reason.
paragraphs.simple: Ruby thinks Hawk is friendly to her because he expects her to die soon. As a son, he can never be queen, so he is safe.

paragraphs.context: Ruby’s breath caught in her throat at the sight of
paragraphs.simple: Burn stands beside Scarlet, looking bored and disgusted. Ruby finds it hard to call her a queen.

paragraphs.context: “You may all have heard of a certain … prophecy,”
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet talks about the prophecy. The dragonets of the prophecy will hatch tonight unless something terrible happens.

paragraphs.context: “I know,” said Queen Scarlet. “A nasty IceWing thief got
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet says an IceWing thief stole the biggest SkyWing egg from the hatchery last night.

background.note: Silver-white or pale blue dragons from the frozen north of Pyrrhia. They can live in great cold and breathe out a deadly freezing breath (frostbreath).

paragraphs.context: The air crackled as if it might burst into flames
paragraphs.simple: Ruby thinks a SkyWing could not survive in the Ice Kingdom.

background.note: The land of the SkyWings, high in the mountains.
The cold, snowy land of the IceWings in the far north.

paragraphs.context: So was he one of the Talons of Peace? Were
paragraphs.simple: Ruby wonders if the thief was gathering the dragonets of the prophecy.

background.note: The five dragonets of the prophecy: Clay, Tsunami, Glory, Starflight and Sunny. 'Destiny' means what is sure to happen in the future.

paragraphs.context: “Oh, don’t worry,” her mother said. “Queen Burn chased him
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet says Burn killed the thief and destroyed the egg. Now they will make sure no SkyWing hatches on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: Ruby watched in confusion as seven guards filed in, each
paragraphs.simple: Seven guards bring in eggs that are already starting to hatch.

paragraphs.context: There’s something alive in there, Ruby thought, and then suddenly
paragraphs.simple: A little head pops out of the rocks. Scarlet jumps back, and Ruby sees fear in her eyes.

paragraphs.context: It looked like an ordinary dragonet — about a year
paragraphs.simple: It looks like a normal young dragonet with bright copper scales.

paragraphs.context: The weirdest, creepiest blue Ruby had ever seen, far beyond
paragraphs.simple: Her eyes are a strange, burning blue, and smoke rises from her scales.

paragraphs.context: Ruby had a dim memory now of something that had
paragraphs.simple: Ruby remembers that over a year ago an egg hatched with twins inside, and the mother tried to escape with them.

paragraphs.context: “Your Majesty,” said a squat rust-colored dragon near the front
paragraphs.simple: An old advisor speaks up. Ruby and Tourmaline called him "Kidney Breath" because he always talked about eating goat kidneys.

paragraphs.context: Queen Scarlet gave him a glittering, all-teeth smile. “Does it
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet calls the dragonet her dangerous new toy and her future champion.

paragraphs.context: “She’s not just any monster,” Scarlet said smugly. “She’s my
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet calls the dragonet her useful monster and hands her an egg, carefully not touching her.

paragraphs.context: The dragonet looked down at the egg, which was almost
paragraphs.simple: The dragonet looks curious and happy, as if nobody had ever given her a present.

paragraphs.context: And then small tremors began to run across the eggshell
paragraphs.simple: The egg turns gray, then black, and the dragonet inside it dies.

paragraphs.context: Scarlet reached over with the scepter and knocked down the
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet orders the dragonet, Peril, to touch the rest of the eggs.

background.note: Peril is a SkyWing with firescales: her scales are so hot that they burn anything she touches.

paragraphs.context: She could do that to anyone, Ruby realized. She can
paragraphs.simple: Ruby realizes Peril could kill any dragon just by touching it.

paragraphs.context: Scarlet was watching Ruby with a satisfied, sinister look. A
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet's look tells Ruby: if you ever try to challenge me, Peril will come for you.

paragraphs.context: So I won’t, Ruby thought. I won’t dream of the
paragraphs.simple: Ruby decides never to want the throne. She will be obedient to stay alive.

paragraphs.context: The dragonet lifted her claws from the last smoking egg
paragraphs.simple: Peril looks at Scarlet the way a child looks at a parent, hoping to be loved.

paragraphs.context: Deep in a cave in Jade Mountain, the most dangerous
paragraphs.simple: Years later, Peril is hiding in a cave inside Jade Mountain, and she does not like it.

background.note: A tall mountain in the middle of Pyrrhia with many caves inside it.
The large land (continent) where all the dragon tribes in these books live.

paragraphs.context: “Just until Ruby’s gone,” Peril muttered, pacing. “That’s what he
paragraphs.simple: Peril is waiting until Ruby leaves. She says she is not afraid of anyone.

background.note: The dragon world has three moons. Dragons say 'Three moons!' when they are surprised or upset, the way people say 'Oh my goodness!'

paragraphs.context: Yes, she was banished from the Sky Kingdom, but Queen
paragraphs.simple: Ruby banished Peril from the Sky Kingdom, but Clay said Peril has every right to be at Jade Mountain.

background.note: Clay is a MudWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is big, kind and loyal.

paragraphs.context: But all she wanted was to be with Clay. Near
paragraphs.simple: Peril only wants to be near Clay. If she is not hurting anyone, why should that be a problem?

paragraphs.context: Well. Peril hissed a tendril of smoke and marched to
paragraphs.simple: If anyone tried to keep her away from Clay, Peril would melt their head off — unless Clay told her not to.

paragraphs.context: There had been a moment, months ago, in the chaos
paragraphs.simple: After Peril helped Clay escape from Scarlet's arena, Scarlet and Burn were gone and the SkyWings were in panic.

paragraphs.context: The relief when Princess Ruby arrived and took over …
paragraphs.simple: When Ruby took over, Peril hoped everything would change.

paragraphs.context: It was true: everything had changed. For the better, generally
paragraphs.simple: Things did change, but not for Peril. Nobody thanked her for helping.

paragraphs.context: Instead, Ruby’s very first act as queen had been to
paragraphs.simple: Ruby's first act as queen was to banish Peril.

paragraphs.context: Until that moment, Ruby had always been — not friendly
paragraphs.simple: Ruby used to be quiet and stay out of Peril's way. Now she is a strong, decisive queen.

paragraphs.context: “Because you’re a murderer,” Ruby replied, as if that should
paragraphs.simple: Ruby said Peril must leave because she is a murderer.

paragraphs.context: But aren’t we all murderers? Peril had thought. Didn’t we
paragraphs.simple: Peril thinks everyone did terrible things for Scarlet. Why is only she being punished?

paragraphs.context: Then she’d looked into Ruby’s eyes and realized it was
paragraphs.simple: Peril sees that Ruby truly hates her, but she does not know why.

paragraphs.context: And how do you plan to make me? Peril had
paragraphs.simple: Peril was so angry she could have burned everyone in the cave.

paragraphs.context: She nearly had. She’d really, really wanted to. The only
paragraphs.simple: Only the thought of Clay stopped her. He believes she can be good, so she will try.

paragraphs.context: And she didn’t like being told to sit in a
paragraphs.simple: Ruby is coming to Jade Mountain to collect the body of a student who died, Carnelian.

background.note: Carnelian is a SkyWing student at Jade Mountain Academy. She is often angry.

paragraphs.context: Farther along the tunnel, deeper in the mountain, the faint
paragraphs.simple: Peril hears SeaWing students playing at the underground lake. She avoids all the students.

background.note: Blue or green dragons who live in the sea. They can breathe underwater, and the stripes on their scales glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Everyone here was afraid of her, but no one was
paragraphs.simple: In the Sky Palace, everyone knew to keep away from Peril. Here the students forget she is there, so she must be careful.

paragraphs.context: He said she deserved a second chance … but if
paragraphs.simple: Clay gave Peril a second chance. If she burned one of his students, there would not be another.

paragraphs.context: Didn’t matter. They still hated her, those shining friends who
paragraphs.simple: Clay's friends do not trust Peril and watch her whenever she is near him.

paragraphs.context: Down on the sands of Burn’s stronghold, after she’d saved
paragraphs.simple: After Peril saved Clay, he said, "Maybe Peril is our wings of fire." She hoped this would make up for everything.

paragraphs.context: After the end of the war, Peril had searched for
paragraphs.simple: After the war, Peril searched for Scarlet everywhere. Dragons screamed, fainted or threw things at her.

background.note: Big, strong brown dragons who live in the swamps of the Mud Kingdom. They can hold their breath for up to an hour and hide in mud.

paragraphs.context: It was strange to realize that a dragon who couldn’t
paragraphs.simple: Peril cannot be hurt on the outside, but she has many painful holes on the inside.

paragraphs.context: The dark green SeaWing dragonet didn’t scream or faint or
paragraphs.simple: A dark green SeaWing almost bumps into her. He does not scream; he just closes his eyes.

paragraphs.context: What a peculiar dragon. He seemed to have no fire
paragraphs.simple: Peril thinks of Tsunami and her little sister as full of fire. This SeaWing seems calm and quiet, like a puddle.

background.note: Tsunami is a SeaWing princess, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is brave and likes to be the leader.

paragraphs.context: “Who are you?” she asked. Hmmm. That came out more
paragraphs.simple: Peril tries to sound nice and ends up talking nervously about not having a murder list.

paragraphs.context: “I just did what I was told,” she said in
paragraphs.mainIdea: "I just did what I was told."
paragraphs.simple: Peril says she only did what her queen ordered. Can she help what she is like?

paragraphs.context: His green-eyed gaze traveled thoughtfully along her smoking scales, shifted
paragraphs.simple: The SeaWing tells her his name is Turtle. At first Peril thinks he is calling her a turtle.

background.note: Turtle is a quiet SeaWing prince and a student at Jade Mountain Academy. He is Tsunami's brother.

paragraphs.context: “Oh!” she said. “Right. Hello. Thank you for not screaming
paragraphs.simple: Peril thanks him for not screaming, fainting or throwing a crocodile at her.

paragraphs.context: But before he could answer, a roar billowed down through
paragraphs.simple: A roar echoes through the mountain. Peril thinks it is probably Queen Ruby.

paragraphs.context: “I don’t mean go say hi,” Turtle protested. “I mean
paragraphs.simple: Turtle wants to listen secretly and asks Peril to come.

paragraphs.context: That sounded true. That sounded very true! Really, Clay just
paragraphs.simple: Peril decides that if Ruby does not see her, it is almost the same as staying out of the way.

paragraphs.context: On the one talon, she was still pretty sure Clay
paragraphs.simple: Peril thinks about the choice "on one talon … on the other talon …", and on a third and fourth talon too.

paragraphs.context: Unless Clay secretly thought she was too dangerous for anyone
paragraphs.simple: Her only friend before Clay was killed by Scarlet for telling Peril too much.

paragraphs.context: But if she had Clay and Turtle as friends, and
paragraphs.simple: Peril thinks that if Turtle is killed, she will still have Clay. Then she realizes this is a morbid way to think about a new friend.

paragraphs.context: For the past week, Carnelian’s body had been kept in
paragraphs.simple: Carnelian's body has been kept near the top of the mountain. SkyWings leave their dead open to the sky for seven days so their spirits can fly free.

background.note: Osprey is an old SkyWing in the Sky Palace, the only one who would talk to Peril.

paragraphs.context: That kind of talk always made Queen Scarlet roll her
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet lets her tribe keep their customs, but she is not interested in what happens after death.

paragraphs.context: Peril had visited the body twice, at night when everyone
paragraphs.simple: Peril visited the body twice at night. She did not know Carnelian; Scarlet did not like Peril talking to other dragons.

paragraphs.context: But she hadn’t seen the cave in the daytime before.
paragraphs.simple: In the sunlight, the cave looks beautiful, and the wind moves the silk as if Carnelian were breathing.

paragraphs.context: Unless it was scared off by the angry dragons gathered
paragraphs.simple: Angry dragons are shouting around the body, so nobody hears Turtle and Peril sneaking closer.

paragraphs.context: “I smell lies all over this story,” snarled a SkyWing
paragraphs.simple: A SkyWing says Carnelian died exactly the way Peril's victims die. He calls Peril a bloodthirsty criminal.

paragraphs.context: Oh — that’s me, Peril realized. I’m the violent, bloodthirsty
paragraphs.simple: Peril is offended. She does not kill for fun, and she has not killed anyone in months.

paragraphs.context: The unfamiliar SkyWing hissed with disbelief. “What sounds more likely
paragraphs.simple: The SkyWing asks: did Scarlet's monster kill Carnelian, or did a MudWing set off a bomb by accident?

paragraphs.context: “I want to know where the MudWing is.” Queen Ruby’s
paragraphs.simple: Ruby wants to know where the MudWing is. Peril cannot tell what Ruby is feeling.

paragraphs.context: Peril coiled into herself, remembering the weight of the dragonet
paragraphs.simple: Peril remembers pulling Carnelian out of the burning cave, too late. She wonders if saving her would have changed anything.

paragraphs.context: “Peril pulled Carnelian out of the fire,” Sunny said, her
paragraphs.simple: Sunny says Peril's talon prints are on the body because Peril tried to save Carnelian.

background.note: Sunny is a small SandWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is cheerful and always hopes for the best.

paragraphs.context: “Sora.” That was Clay! It felt like wings spreading inside
paragraphs.simple: Clay says the MudWing who escaped is Sora, his sister. He sounds very sad.

background.note: Sora is Clay's sister, a MudWing.

paragraphs.context: He sounded so, so sad. Peril wanted to burst into
paragraphs.simple: Peril wants to hug Clay, and then burn the SkyWings who are being mean to him.

paragraphs.context: “Queen Moorhen has agreed to meet with you,” Sunny said
paragraphs.simple: Sunny says the MudWing queen will meet Ruby and help her find justice.

background.note: Queen Moorhen is the queen of the MudWings.

paragraphs.context: Peril always thought of Clay’s soul as a torch that
paragraphs.simple: Peril thinks of Clay's soul as a torch. Sunny is like too-bright sunlight that gives her a headache.

paragraphs.context: (Peril knew this was bad. Sunny was the only one
paragraphs.simple: Sunny is the only one of Clay's friends who is nice to Peril, but Peril still sometimes dreams of having Clay all to herself.

background.note: Dragons of the rainforest whose scales change colour. They can hide by matching the colours around them, and they can shoot venom from their fangs.

paragraphs.context: “No,” said the watcher. “I see orange scales … ”
paragraphs.simple: A watcher sees a dragon with orange scales coming. A wave of horror spreads through the cave.

paragraphs.context: It was the night after Peril had freed Scarlet from
paragraphs.simple: Peril remembers the night after she freed Scarlet from Burn's tower. They sat by a fire in the wasteland.

background.note: The desert land of the SandWings.

paragraphs.context: “I don’t think she will,” Peril said. “She’s made a
paragraphs.mainIdea: Ruby is stronger than she seems.
paragraphs.simple: Peril says Ruby has made many changes and banished Peril. She is scarier than Scarlet thinks.

background.note: A palace of Queen Coral in the Kingdom of the Sea. SkyWings attacked and destroyed it in book 2.

paragraphs.context: “She’s not,” Peril said. Truthfully, Peril wasn’t sure what Ruby
paragraphs.simple: Peril partly wants to hurt Scarlet and scare her away from the palace, to keep Clay safe.

paragraphs.context: Scarlet unconsciously reached one talon toward her scarred face, but
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet's face was burned by venom, and her time in Burn's tower took away some of her confidence.

background.note: Poison made by an animal. RainWings can shoot venom from their fangs that melts whatever it hits; SandWings have poison in the barb on their tail.

paragraphs.context: “No,” Scarlet said. “I have a better idea.” She bared
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet tells Peril to go back to the Sky Palace and kill Ruby.

paragraphs.context: “Well, I’m not going to kill her,” Peril said. “You
paragraphs.simple: Peril says she will not kill for Scarlet anymore. She is not that kind of dragon now.

paragraphs.context: Scarlet’s eyes narrowed. “Oh, really? You think you’ve changed so
paragraphs.simple: Scarlet says Peril was born to burn enemies and has always enjoyed it.

paragraphs.context: “I don’t have to be,” Peril said stubbornly. “Clay says
paragraphs.simple: Peril says Clay thinks she can be whoever she wants. She knows at once it was a mistake to mention him.

paragraphs.context: Peril couldn’t believe the stab of dismay that made her
paragraphs.simple: Peril hates that she still wants Scarlet to like her.

paragraphs.context: Peril poked her claw into a scorched circle of grass
paragraphs.simple: Peril wonders if she could trade Ruby's life for Clay's safety.

paragraphs.context: But, for one thing, she couldn’t trust Scarlet to keep
paragraphs.simple: But she cannot trust Scarlet, and Clay would be disappointed in her.

paragraphs.context: The next morning, Scarlet was gone. Peril had not been

parts.text: The halls were quieter than she remembered them being,
parts.meaning: The hallways were quieter than before,

parts.text: and there was a general hush over the palace,
parts.meaning: and the whole palace was silent,

parts.text: as if half the dragons were in hiding,
parts.meaning: as though many dragons were hiding,

parts.text: waiting for something to change.
parts.meaning: waiting for things to change.

sentences.grammar: "Quieter than" is a comparative. "As if" introduces how things seemed.

sentences.context: Something was shaking at the corners of Peril’s brain, shaking and tugging and pulling and trying to come loose, but she couldn’t sink her teeth into it … she couldn’t remember …
sentences.simple: A memory was trying to come back to Peril, but she couldn't catch it.

parts.text: Something was shaking at the corners of Peril’s brain,
parts.meaning: Something was moving at the edge of Peril's mind,

parts.text: shaking and tugging and pulling and trying to come loose,
parts.meaning: pulling and trying to break free,

parts.text: but she couldn’t sink her teeth into it …
parts.meaning: but she couldn't catch hold of it…

parts.text: she couldn’t remember …
parts.meaning: she couldn't remember…

sentences.grammar: "Sink your teeth into something" means take a firm hold of it. Many "-ing" verbs make the struggle feel long.

sentences.context: The daylight had a smoky green tinge to it, as if the sky, too, knew that something was wrong … something was unbalanced in the world below.
sentences.simple: The light looked slightly green and smoky, as if even the sky knew something was wrong.

parts.text: The daylight had a smoky green tinge to it,
parts.meaning: The light looked a little green and smoky,

parts.text: as if the sky, too, knew that something was wrong …
parts.meaning: as though even the sky could tell something was wrong…

parts.text: something was unbalanced in the world below.
parts.meaning: something was out of balance in the world.

sentences.grammar: "A tinge" is a small amount of a color. "Too" between commas means "also".

sentences.context: The same green all the time — no camouflage, no flamboyant emotional outbursts, no self-absorbed displays of clever special effects.
sentences.simple: He was always the same green: no hiding colors, no showy feelings, no clever tricks.

parts.text: The same green all the time —
parts.meaning: Always the same green color —

parts.text: no camouflage,
parts.meaning: no hiding by changing color,

parts.text: no flamboyant emotional outbursts,
parts.meaning: no bright colors showing strong feelings,

parts.text: no self-absorbed displays of clever special effects.
parts.meaning: no proud shows of clever color tricks.

sentences.grammar: This is not a full sentence: it has no main verb. The dash introduces a list of three "no…" phrases.

sentences.context: As they soared up the cliffside, Peril had a dizzying sense of déjà vu — a feeling of wild freedom, terror, and hope that didn’t match the current situation at all.
sentences.simple: Flying up the cliff, Peril strongly felt she had done this before, with feelings of freedom, fear and hope that didn't fit now.

parts.text: As they soared up the cliffside,
parts.meaning: While they flew up the cliff,

parts.text: Peril had a dizzying sense of déjà vu —
parts.meaning: Peril strongly felt she had lived this before —

parts.text: a feeling of wild freedom, terror, and hope
parts.meaning: a feeling of freedom, fear and hope

parts.text: that didn’t match the current situation at all.
parts.meaning: that did not fit what was happening now.

sentences.grammar: "Déjà vu" (French) is the feeling that something has happened before. The dash introduces an explanation.

sentences.context: Queen Scarlet could never hit her, of course, but she’d found plenty of other ways to make Peril’s life miserable.
sentences.simple: Scarlet could not touch Peril, but she had many other ways to make her unhappy.

parts.text: Queen Scarlet could never hit her, of course,
parts.meaning: Of course, Scarlet could not hit her,

parts.text: but she’d found plenty of other ways
parts.meaning: but she had found many other ways

parts.text: to make Peril’s life miserable.
parts.meaning: to make Peril very unhappy.

sentences.grammar: "She'd found" = "she had found" (past perfect). "Of course" shows the reader already knows why.

sentences.context: The two SkyWing queens took off first, soaring toward the sky, and then what seemed to be the entire palace lifted off to follow them, dragons jostling for airspace as they competed for a ringside seat at the fight.
sentences.simple: The two queens flew up first, then almost the whole palace followed, pushing each other to get the best view of the fight.

parts.text: The two SkyWing queens took off first,
parts.meaning: The two queens flew up first,

parts.text: soaring toward the sky,
parts.meaning: rising high,

parts.text: and then what seemed to be the entire palace lifted off to follow them,
parts.meaning: and then almost everyone in the palace flew after them,

parts.text: dragons jostling for airspace
parts.meaning: dragons pushing each other for space

parts.text: as they competed for a ringside seat at the fight.
parts.meaning: as they tried to get the best place to watch.

sentences.grammar: "What seemed to be" means "something that looked like". "A ringside seat" is a seat right next to a fight.

sentences.context: Scarlet’s blood had almost turned her scales back to red, but the rain spilled over her wings and back, revealing Tourmaline’s unfamiliar orange again.
sentences.simple: Scarlet's blood had made her look red again, but the rain washed it off and showed Tourmaline's orange scales.
sentences.main: The rain shows her true colors.

parts.text: Scarlet’s blood had almost turned her scales back to red,
parts.meaning: Scarlet's blood had nearly made her scales red again,

parts.text: but the rain spilled over her wings and back,
parts.meaning: but rain poured over her,

parts.text: revealing Tourmaline’s unfamiliar orange again.
parts.meaning: showing Tourmaline's new orange color.

sentences.grammar: "Revealing…" shows the result of the rain. "Turned … back to" means changed again to an earlier state.

sentences.context: She thought about Clay, and loyalty, and everything he’d ever said about the family you make and the dragons you should trust and how to make the world safer for everyone.
sentences.simple: She thought about Clay and all he said about chosen family, trust and making the world safer.

parts.text: She thought about Clay, and loyalty,
parts.meaning: She thought about Clay and about being loyal,

parts.text: and everything he’d ever said
parts.meaning: and all the things Clay had said

parts.text: about the family you make and the dragons you should trust
parts.meaning: about the family you choose and whom to trust

parts.text: and how to make the world safer for everyone.
parts.meaning: and how to make the world safer.

sentences.grammar: "You" here means people in general. "The family you make" = friends who become your family.

sentences.context: She drew Cliff closer under her wing; he’d insisted on staying up till midnight, and he looked a lot more awake than Turtle, who kept yawning and leaning on things.
sentences.simple: Ruby pulled Cliff close; he wanted to stay up until midnight and looked more awake than sleepy Turtle.

parts.text: She drew Cliff closer under her wing;
parts.meaning: Ruby pulled Cliff closer under her wing;

parts.text: he’d insisted on staying up till midnight,
parts.meaning: he had demanded to stay awake until midnight,

parts.text: and he looked a lot more awake than Turtle,
parts.meaning: and he looked much less sleepy than Turtle,

parts.text: who kept yawning and leaning on things.
parts.meaning: who was yawning and leaning on things all the time.

sentences.grammar: "Insist on + -ing" = demand to do something. "Kept + -ing" = did again and again.

sentences.context: Such as find her father, get that scroll into talons that could be trusted, and maybe help Turtle and his friends stop some big new terrible prophecy, if they’d have her.
sentences.simple: For example, find her father, give the scroll to trustworthy dragons, and maybe help Turtle's friends with a new prophecy, if they wanted her.

parts.text: Such as find her father,
parts.meaning: For example, find her father,

parts.text: get that scroll into talons that could be trusted,
parts.meaning: give the scroll to dragons who can be trusted,

parts.text: and maybe help Turtle and his friends stop some big new terrible prophecy,
parts.meaning: and perhaps help Turtle's group stop a new frightening prophecy,

parts.text: if they’d have her.
parts.meaning: if they would accept her.

sentences.grammar: This starts with "Such as", continuing the list of "important things" from the sentence before. "Have her" = accept her in the group.

sentences.context: He just has to take it off, and all the wounds disappear — then when he puts it back on, the scroll makes him a NightWing per the instructions all over again.
sentences.simple: When he takes off the shape, his wounds disappear; when he puts it on again, the scroll makes a fresh NightWing.

parts.text: He just has to take it off,
parts.meaning: He only needs to remove it,

parts.text: and all the wounds disappear —
parts.meaning: and all his injuries are gone —

parts.text: then when he puts it back on,
parts.meaning: then when he wears it again,

parts.text: the scroll makes him a NightWing per the instructions all over again.
parts.meaning: the scroll makes him a new NightWing exactly as the spell says.

sentences.grammar: "Per the instructions" = following the instructions. Present tense explains how something always works.

sentences.context: She knew what it was like to wish for different scales, and she knew how much he needed them, as a RainWing with no scale-shifting powers.
sentences.simple: Peril understood wanting different scales, and she knew how much he needed his shapes, being a RainWing who can't change color.

parts.text: She knew what it was like to wish for different scales,
parts.meaning: She understood the wish for different scales,

parts.text: and she knew how much he needed them,
parts.meaning: and she knew how important they were to him,

parts.text: as a RainWing with no scale-shifting powers.
parts.meaning: because he was a RainWing who couldn't change color.

sentences.grammar: "What it was like" means how it felt. "As a…" here means "because he is a…".

sentences.context: For a moment, the sheath hovered in the air, as if considering whether to listen to her, and then it spun slowly and floated over to land in Turtle’s talons.
sentences.simple: The case floated for a moment as though it was thinking, then turned and landed in Turtle's claws.

parts.text: For a moment, the sheath hovered in the air,
parts.meaning: For a short time, the case stayed in the air,

parts.text: as if considering whether to listen to her,
parts.meaning: as though it was deciding whether to obey her,

parts.text: and then it spun slowly and floated over
parts.meaning: and then it turned slowly and drifted across

parts.text: to land in Turtle’s talons.
parts.meaning: and landed in Turtle's claws.

sentences.grammar: "As if considering" shows how it seemed. "Whether" introduces a choice (yes or no).

sentences.context: Not that she wanted to use her firescales on Moon, but if the alternative was some big ancient nightmare dragon rising from the earth, then shouldn’t all the options be open?
sentences.simple: She didn't want to burn Moon, but if the other choice was a terrible old dragon getting free, shouldn't she be allowed to?

parts.text: Not that she wanted to use her firescales on Moon,
parts.meaning: She did not really want to burn Moon,

parts.text: but if the alternative was some big ancient nightmare dragon rising from the earth,
parts.meaning: but if the other choice was a terrible old dragon coming out of the ground,

parts.text: then shouldn’t all the options be open?
parts.meaning: then surely every choice should be allowed?

sentences.grammar: "Not that…" means "I don't mean that…". "The alternative" is the other possible choice.

sentences.context: Peril sidled to the edge of the boulder, hopped down onto the grass, hurried through the scorched path she made toward the fighting dragons, and paused right behind Qibli.
sentences.simple: Peril moved quietly off the boulder, walked quickly toward the fighting dragons, burning a path, and stopped behind Qibli.

parts.text: Peril sidled to the edge of the boulder,
parts.meaning: Peril moved sideways quietly to the edge of the rock,

parts.text: hopped down onto the grass,
parts.meaning: jumped down onto the grass,

parts.text: hurried through the scorched path she made toward the fighting dragons,
parts.meaning: rushed toward the fighting dragons, burning the grass as she went,

parts.text: and paused right behind Qibli.
parts.meaning: and stopped just behind Qibli.

sentences.grammar: Four past-tense verbs in a row (sidled, hopped, hurried, paused) show quick actions in order.

sentences.context: Moon’s expression was all relief as well, so, despite the shock on Winter and Qibli’s faces, Peril felt a sudden, clear bolt of that was the right thing to do.
sentences.simple: Moon looked relieved too, so even though Winter and Qibli were shocked, Peril suddenly felt sure she had done the right thing.

parts.text: Moon’s expression was all relief as well,
parts.meaning: Moon also looked completely relieved,

parts.text: so, despite the shock on Winter and Qibli’s faces,
parts.meaning: so although Winter and Qibli looked shocked,

parts.text: Peril felt a sudden, clear bolt of
parts.meaning: Peril suddenly and clearly felt

parts.text: that was the right thing to do.
parts.meaning: that she had done the right thing.

sentences.grammar: The thought "that was the right thing to do" is used like a noun after "a bolt of". "Despite" + noun = even with.

sentences.context: He wasn’t sure how long he’d been in there, since he no longer needed light to work by.
sentences.simple: He did not know how long he had been there, because he did not need light for his work any more.
sentences.main: Starflight has lost track of time.

parts.text: He wasn’t sure how long he’d been in there,
parts.meaning: He did not know how long he had been there,

parts.text: since he no longer needed light to work by.
parts.meaning: because he did not need light for his work any more.

sentences.grammar: "Since" here means "because". "Light to work by" = light that helps you see while you work.

sentences.context: Small talonsteps, light — but not Kinkajou — with an extra flap sound when they hit the floor.
sentences.simple: He hears small, light dragon steps, not Kinkajou's, with a flapping sound each time a foot touches the floor.

parts.text: Small talonsteps, light —
parts.meaning: Small, light dragon steps —

parts.text: but not Kinkajou —
parts.meaning: but not Kinkajou's steps —

parts.text: with an extra flap sound when they hit the floor.
parts.meaning: with a flapping sound each time a foot touches the floor.

sentences.grammar: This is not a full sentence. It shows Starflight's quick thoughts while he listens.

sentences.context: It sounded as if she put one talon on the translucent leaves and stood for a moment quietly, without speaking.
sentences.simple: From the sounds, it seemed that she put one foot on the thin leaves of the window and stood still for a short time, saying nothing.
sentences.main: Anemone stands quietly at the window.

parts.text: It sounded as if
parts.meaning: From the sounds, it seemed that

parts.text: she put one talon on the translucent leaves
parts.meaning: she put one foot on the thin leaves of the window

parts.text: and stood for a moment quietly, without speaking.
parts.meaning: and stood still for a short time, saying nothing.

sentences.grammar: "As if" tells us what seems true. Starflight cannot see, so he guesses from the sounds.

sentences.context: “Something that shook the earth,” she said at last, so softly that he wondered if he would have been able to hear her before, when he could see.
sentences.simple: Anemone finally said that something shook the ground. She spoke so quietly that Starflight asked himself whether he could have heard her in the past, when he could see.

parts.text: “Something that shook the earth,”
parts.meaning: “Something that made the ground shake,”

parts.text: she said at last,
parts.meaning: she finally said,

parts.text: so softly that he wondered
parts.meaning: so quietly that he asked himself

parts.text: if he would have been able to hear her before, when he could see.
parts.meaning: whether he could have heard her in the past, when he could still see.

sentences.grammar: "So softly that…" shows a result. "Would have been able to" talks about something in the past that did not really happen.

a bunch of.meaning: A lot of; a group of.
a bunch of.example: “I’ll just wait for a bunch of eggs that haven’t even hatched yet to save us.
a bunch of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

a couple of.example: “But I should have remembered … it was only a couple of months before the whole catastrophe.”
a couple of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

about to.meaning: Going to happen or do something very soon.
about to.example: They were about to fly over the curve where it veered east and then north again.
about to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

according to.meaning: As said or shown by someone or something.
according to.example: According to SkyWing tradition, their dead were offered to the sky for seven days before being burned.
according to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

after all.meaning: In the end, even though you did not expect it.
after all.example: We don’t particularly like tiny little heroes, after all.
after all.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

all along.meaning: 1. Along the whole length of something ("spikes bristling all along his back"). 2. The whole time, from the beginning.
all along.example: she could see there were dragons yelling and screaming all along the bank and more flapping in from the rooftops.
all along.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

all of a sudden.example: And then, all of a sudden, the river exploded.
all of a sudden.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

all the way.example: “A nasty IceWing thief got all the way in here and actually escaped with an egg — the largest one in the hatchery, as it happens.”
all the way.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

apart from.example: “Apart from the disturbing news about my mother’s new ally?”
apart from.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

as far as.meaning: "As far as she could tell" = from what she could see or know.
as far as.example: It was a room Peril had never been to, as far as she could remember, and she flew after Scarlet, puzzling over what it could be.
as far as.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

as if.meaning: In a way that makes it seem that...
as if.example: The air crackled as if it might burst into flames at any moment.
as if.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

as long as.meaning: If; only if. (Also: for the whole time that.)
as long as.example: As long as Clay was not in immediate danger, maybe she should wait to see what happened before joining in.
as long as.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

as soon as.example: He said he’d come get me as soon as it was safe.
as soon as.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

as though.meaning: In a way that makes it seem that something is true.
as though.example: Her squadron was still here, training and hunting as though nothing odd had happened.
as though.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

at all.meaning: Used with "not", "no", "hardly" or in questions to mean "in any way" or "even a little". "Not at all" = not in any way.
at all.example: In fact, there hadn’t been any acknowledgment at all that Peril had helped the dragonets of destiny defeat Queen Scarlet.
at all.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

at first.meaning: At the start, before something changes.
at first.example: Sunny was sobbing too hard to notice her, and at first, Clay didn’t seem to see her either.
at first.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

at last.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

at least.meaning: Used to say one thing is good, even when other things are bad.
at least.example: At least … she made it look casual, but Ruby could see how
at least.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

at once.meaning: Immediately; or all at the same time.
at once.example: All these thoughts flashed through her head at once, making Peril hesitate long enough to realize that Scarlet wasn’t attacking Soar.
at once.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

at the same time.example: How did dragons focus on staying aloft and attacking and defending all at the same time?
at the same time.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

back and forth.meaning: First one way, then the other way, again and again.
back and forth.example: He rolled his shoulders back and forth, stretching his neck and making agonized faces at his sore muscles.
back and forth.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

be supposed to.meaning: Should; to be expected to do something.
be supposed to.example: He wasn’t supposed to use it WILLY-NILLY on dragons who hated her.
be supposed to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

big deal.meaning: Something important. "No big deal" = not important; nothing to worry about.
big deal.example: It’s really not a big deal.”
big deal.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

burst into.meaning: 1. "Burst into flames" = suddenly start to burn ("It instantly burst into flames"). 2. To come into a place suddenly and fast. "Burst into tears" = suddenly start to cry.
burst into.example: The air crackled as if it might burst into flames at any moment.
burst into.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

by all the moons.meaning: A dragon exclamation, like "For goodness' sake!"
by all the moons.example: everything and tell him where his friends were, but by all the moons, if he couldn’t even handle landing to have a civil
by all the moons.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

by the way.meaning: You say "by the way" to start talking about something new.
by the way.example: That was a plan, by the way, that was never going to happen on Peril’s watch.)
by the way.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

calm down.meaning: To become calm, not excited or afraid.
calm down.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

catch up.meaning: 1. To come up to someone who is in front of you, by going faster. 2. To catch someone up in your arms = to lift them quickly and hold them ("caught her son up in her arms").
catch up.example: because a SeaWing dragonet like her could never possibly catch up with a full-grown SkyWing like Scarlet.
catch up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

change your mind.meaning: To make a different choice from before.
change your mind.example: Did Tourmaline change her mind and run away?
change your mind.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

chime in.meaning: To join a talk by saying something.
chime in.example: Winter suddenly chimed in, then cut himself off with a growl, lashing his tail.
chime in.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

clear your throat.meaning: To cough a little before you speak.
clear your throat.example: The guard in the doorway cleared his throat.
clear your throat.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

come on.example: Winter, come on, don’t pass out.
come on.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

come true.meaning: (Of a wish or dream) to really happen.
come true.example: she couldn’t help it: she still kind of believed it could come true.
come true.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

come up with.meaning: To think of an idea or plan.
come up with.example: Maybe you can help me come up with clever uses for the scroll.
come up with.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

deal with.meaning: To take action to handle a problem or a difficult feeling.
deal with.example: “Now deal with the rest of them, or let me smash them myself.”
deal with.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

each other.meaning: Used to say that each one does something to the other one.
each other.example: The last time they’d seen each other he’d been hopeful … he could see another possible future for her.
each other.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

end up.meaning: To be in a place or situation at the end, often without planning it.
end up.example: You still end up banished from your own home.”
end up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

even if.meaning: It does not matter if this happens; the result is the same.
even if.example: They must have known Tourmaline was missing, even if no one would talk about it.
even if.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

even though.meaning: Although; in spite of the fact that.
even though.example: Even though they were terrified of her, the other students kept forgetting she was there.
even though.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

fall asleep.example: Long after midnight, Queen Scarlet curled her tail in and fell asleep on her throne.
fall asleep.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

fall silent.meaning: To stop talking or stop making noise.
fall silent.example: The queen’s voice lilted over all the others, and the room fell silent.
fall silent.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

feel like.meaning: To seem like; to give a certain feeling. "Feel like doing something" = want to do it.
feel like.example: It felt like walking into a funeral pyre; oppressive heat and the
feel like.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

figure out.meaning: To find the answer to something by thinking.
figure out.example: a dragon loyal to Queen Ruby, or that some MudWing figured out how to set off a dragonflame bomb and accidentally killed
figure out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

find out.meaning: To learn a fact that you did not know.
find out.example: If she found out that Tourmaline was planning to challenge her …
find out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

for a moment.example: Her sister hovered in front of her for a moment.
for a moment.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

for instance.example: dragons might say that was a cruel irony, while others, for instance an entire tribe of RainWings, might laugh and laugh for
for instance.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

for sure.example: Who cares what a bunch of Ruby-butt-noses say; NOT ME, that’s for sure.
for sure.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

get away with.meaning: To do something wrong and not be punished for it.
get away with.example: “You can’t threaten my friends like that and get away with it.”
get away with.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

get out of.meaning: To leave a place; or to find a way to avoid doing something. "Get something out of someone" = make them give it or tell it to you ("What are you trying to get out of me now?").
get out of.example: Ruby, if I defeat her and become queen, we can get out of this war.”
get out of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

get rid of.meaning: To make something go away; to be free of it.
get rid of.example: And the only way to do that was to get rid of Queen Scarlet forever.
get rid of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

get used to.meaning: To become comfortable with something new.
get used to.example: I don’t think I could ever get used to eating hot prey.
get used to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

give up.meaning: 1. To stop trying. 2. To give something up = to stop having it, or to hand it over ("I'll give up my kingdom").
give up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

go on.meaning: To continue; to keep talking ("Ruby went on"). "Going on" = happening ("a big fight going on"; "What's going on?" = what is happening?). "Goes on and off" = is put on and taken off.
go on.example: she went on, “I’m not looking for an entourage.
go on.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

grow up.meaning: To change from a child into an adult.
grow up.example: and you’re here to guide me and teach me and help me grow up, because I couldn’t possibly do that on my own.”
grow up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

had better.meaning: Should. "We'd better go" means we should go now. (Different: "had better control" = had control that was better.)
had better.example: most dragonets were confined to the wingery until they had better control of their limbs.
had better.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

hang on.meaning: To hold something tightly. "Hang on!" can also mean "Wait!"
hang on.example: And hang on, why would Turtle be friends with her if she was really Scarlet’s dangerous weapon?
hang on.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

have a feeling.meaning: To think something is true or will happen, without knowing for sure.
have a feeling.example: She had a feeling she wouldn’t be invited along on any diplomatic missions,
have a feeling.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

i bet.example: And coming to kill you, I bet, Peril thought.
i bet.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

i guess.meaning: "I guess" means "I think so, but I am not sure."
i guess.example: Unless Clay told me not to, I guess.
i guess.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

i mean.meaning: You say it when you want to say something again in a better way.
i mean.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

if only.meaning: "If only ..." means "I wish ..." (but it is not true).
if only.example: If only she could do it for him!
if only.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in a way.meaning: In some way, but not completely.
in a way.example: So in a way she was doing something he would approve of.
in a way.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in case.example: “The rest are still looking, but we wanted to come back and make sure you were guarded, in case it was a trick.”
in case.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

in charge.meaning: Being the one who decides and controls things.
in charge.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

in exchange for.meaning: Given or done to pay for something else.
in exchange for.example: She might be willing to take in a strange dragon who offered mysterious power in exchange for treasure.
in exchange for.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in fact.meaning: Really; actually (used to add something true and surprising).
in fact.example: In fact, there hadn’t been any acknowledgment at all that Peril had helped the dragonets of destiny defeat Queen Scarlet.
in fact.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

in front of.example: Her sister hovered in front of her for a moment.
in front of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in the end.example: of touch that she guessed meant, “we’re both SeaWings, so in the end we’ll stick together.”
in the end.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

in the first place.meaning: At the beginning; before anything else.
in the first place.example: Why did he even want to travel with me in the first place?
in the first place.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in the middle of.meaning: In the centre of a place, or during an event.
in the middle of.example: If you even think about it, now you know whose talons will find your throat in the middle of the night.”
in the middle of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in the world.meaning: Used after "how", "what", "where" or "who" to show you are very surprised ("What in the world…?"); or used to make a word stronger ("the most dangerous dragon in the world").
in the world.example: magical way he had of thinking that any other dragons in the world might have open hearts like his.
in the world.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

in your head.example: That came out more menacing than it sounded in my head.
in your head.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

instead of.meaning: In the place of something else.
instead of.example: The tunnel felt too small, as though she were the size of a thousand-year-old dragon instead of just a five-year-old dragonet.
instead of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

keep an eye on.example: Keep an eye on him until I get back.”
keep an eye on.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

keep up.meaning: To go as fast as someone else; to continue doing something.
keep up.example: Turtle said, beating his wings to keep up.
keep up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

kind of.meaning: 1. A type of ("some kind of code"; "the kind of dragon who..."). 2. A little; in some way (informal): "kind of mean".
kind of.example: Wait, no — to be clear, I have no kind of murder list at all.
kind of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

leave alone.meaning: 1. To not touch, change or bother someone or something. 2. To be left alone = to stay there by yourself after the others go ("Peril was left alone with her father" = only she and her father stayed).
leave alone.example: “I gotta practice my ‘no, no, leave me alone’ face, or else everyone want to be with me ALLLLLLS the time.”
leave alone.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

let go of.example: Chameleon yowled with pain, let go of the scroll, and fell back, covering his snout with his talons.
let go of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

let out.meaning: 1. To make a sound, such as a cry or a sigh. 2. A door or roof that lets out onto a place opens onto it ("The roof of the keep let out onto a rocky mountaintop").
let out.example: Ruby let out a hiss, and Peril met her eyes.
let out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

look around.meaning: To look at the things in a place, or to look in all directions.
look around.example: Peril wiped rain from her eyes and looked around.
look around.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

look like.meaning: To seem to be something, because of how it looks.
look like.example: Scarlet jerked back, and Ruby was shocked to see something that looked like a flash of fear in her eyes.
look like.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

make sure.meaning: To check, or to do something, so that you are sure about something.
make sure.example: We’re going to make sure there are no SkyWings hatching on the brightest night.
make sure.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

make up for.meaning: To do something good so that something bad seems less bad.
make up for.example: “But you can make up for what you’ve done.
make up for.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

might as well.meaning: Could just as easily (be); there is no reason not to.
might as well.example: She might as well have called her son “Disappointment.”
might as well.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

no idea.meaning: "Have no idea" means not know at all.
no idea.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

no longer.meaning: Not now, although it was true before.
no longer.example: Peril glanced up and realized the big NightWing was no longer in the sky above them.
no longer.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

no matter what.example: to touch, she would never have dared to stand so close, no matter what Queen Scarlet’s orders were.
no matter what.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

no sign of.meaning: Nothing that shows someone is there.
no sign of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

no way.meaning: 1. That can't be true! 2. Certainly not. 3. "There is no way to..." = it is impossible to...
no way.example: There’s no way to defeat her.”
no way.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

nothing but.example: She’s unpredictable and knows nothing but killing.
nothing but.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

of course.example: That is … unless something simply dreadful happens, of course.”
of course.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

oh, dear.meaning: What you say when you are worried, sorry or a little upset about something. It does not mean "loved" here.
oh, dear.example: “Oh, dear,” Sunny said in a small voice.
oh, dear.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

oh, my.meaning: What you say when you are surprised or shocked, like "Oh!" or "Wow!" Here "my" does not mean "belonging to me". ("Oh my gosh!" and "Oh my goodness!" mean the same.)
oh, my.example: “Oh my,” said the NightWing in the air above them.
oh, my.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

on fire.example: Which probably meant he didn’t want her setting large groups of dragons on fire every time she got mad.
on fire.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

on purpose.meaning: Because you want to; not by accident.
on purpose.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

on your own.meaning: Alone, without help from other people.
on your own.example: to Peril for weeks, and then Peril had to figure out on her own what she’d done wrong and how to fix it to make Queen
on your own.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

one another.example: near the river, in a spot where giant boulders overlapped one another halfway into the water and small rapids bustled noisily
one another.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

one by one.example: One by one, Peril stopped at each egg and laid her claws on it until the dragonet inside was dead.
one by one.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

or else.meaning: Or if not; otherwise. "Or else!" can also be a warning.
or else.example: She couldn’t even think about it, or else the tunnel would soon be full of rage smoke.
or else.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

out loud.meaning: In a voice that other people can hear.
out loud.example: Clay would never say it out loud — he’d never ask her for it directly.
out loud.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

out of the way.meaning: Not standing where someone wants to go.
out of the way.example: it would be easier for Clay and his friends if she stayed out of the way, so that Ruby’s visit would go as smoothly as possible.
out of the way.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

over and over.example: “Poking around inside my brain to find the answer to a question I’ve already answered over and over.
over and over.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

pick up.meaning: 1. To lift something up with your hand. 2. To pick up thoughts = to notice or hear them ("I don't think I could pick up anything from way up here").
pick up.example: He took a deep breath and picked up the head.
pick up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

plenty of.meaning: A lot of; more than enough.
plenty of.example: Peril had been in plenty of fights where her first move was grabbing a SandWing’s tail to burn off the barb at the end.
plenty of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

point out.meaning: To tell someone about something so that they see it or know it.
point out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

rather than.example: He shot out of the way, no doubt congratulating himself on moving so quickly rather than realizing she’d deliberately spared him.
rather than.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

reach out.meaning: To move your hand forward to touch or take something.
reach out.example: Clay’s big MudWing wings trembled as he tried to reach out and touch the severed head.
reach out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

right away.example: She knew right away that mentioning him was a mistake.
right away.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

roll one's eyes.meaning: To move your eyes up and around, to show that you think something is silly.
roll one's eyes.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

run away.meaning: To leave a place secretly or quickly to escape.
run away.example: Did Tourmaline change her mind and run away?
run away.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

run through.meaning: 1. When a feeling runs through you, it goes quickly through all your body ("A jolt ran through her"). Talk can also run through a crowd. 2. To go quickly through a list or a plan, often in your mind.
run through.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

shake your head.meaning: To move your head from side to side to say "no" or to show you are unhappy.
shake your head.example: She shook her head without answering and lifted off into the sky.
shake your head.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

side by side.example: She would never paint huge canvases side by side with other SkyWings and SandWings, dipping their tails
side by side.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

so far.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

someone walking over your grave.meaning: A saying for a sudden cold, scary shiver that comes for no clear reason. Usually people say "someone walked over my grave".
someone walking over your grave.example: “It felt,” she said, “like someone slithering over my grave.”
someone walking over your grave.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

sooner or later.meaning: At some time in the future, even if not soon.
sooner or later.example: I mean, you’d have figured out the truth sooner or later, once you heard from Glory.”
sooner or later.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

sort of.meaning: 1. A little; not completely. (Informal.) 2. A type of; something like ("a sort of nondescript yellowish-green").
sort of.example: But no one knew if they’d found Scarlet, and Peril sort of expected that if they had, they’d all be dead.
sort of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

stay away from.example: “You can’t make me stay away from my friends.”
stay away from.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

step forward.meaning: To move one step to the front.
step forward.example: She stepped forward, and the guards holding the eggs all quickly placed them on the ground, stumbling out of her way.
step forward.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

take a deep breath.meaning: To breathe in a lot of air, often to feel calm.
take a deep breath.example: He took a deep breath, his wings drifting down like falling leaves.
take a deep breath.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

take a step back.meaning: To move back one step, often because you are surprised or afraid.
take a step back.example: One of the dragons was a big red SkyWing, and Peril definitely saw her flinch and take a step back.
take a step back.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

take care of.meaning: To look after someone or something and keep them safe.
take care of.example: “The prophecy will take care of the war,” she argued.
take care of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

take over.example: The relief when Princess Ruby arrived and took over … Peril remembered it clearly, with a wince of pity for her idiotic hopeful former self.
take over.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

tell the truth.meaning: To say what is really true, not a lie.
tell the truth.example: “But if you’d like to find out whether he’s telling the truth, come a bit closer and we can do a fun experiment.”
tell the truth.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

thanks to.example: Probably thanks to me, by the way.
thanks to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

the rest of.example: He’d seen the rest of his sisters die under Scarlet’s claws.
the rest of.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

three moons.meaning: "Three moons!" is an exclamation, like "Oh my goodness!" (It can also mean the three real moons in the dragons' sky.)
three moons.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

to do with.meaning: "Have something to do with" = be connected with something. "What to do with someone" = how to deal with them ("until I figure out what to do with you").
to do with.example: Ruby had time to wonder if the thrilling announcement had anything to do with Tourmaline (“I have thrillingly murdered one daughter!
to do with.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

trail off.meaning: (Of a voice) to slowly become quieter and stop.
trail off.example: He trailed off, perhaps realizing there was no good way to end that sentence.
trail off.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

turn out.meaning: To happen in the end in a way you did not expect. "Turned out to be" means were, as people learned later.
turn out.example: I say it’s no coincidence this one turned out the way she did.
turn out.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

under a spell.example: “Hey, I’m not under a spell,” Peril interjected.
under a spell.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

used to.meaning: Did something regularly in the past, but not now. "Be used to" = know something well, so it is not strange.
used to.example: According to our history, the SkyWing tribe used to kill them the moment we figured out what they were.”
used to.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

wake up.example: “Am I going to wake up on fire one day?
wake up.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to learn.

what if.example: But what if she bumped into one of them?
what if.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

who cares.meaning: It doesn't matter; I don't care. (Different: "the one who cares about you" = the one who loves you and wants good things for you.)
who cares.example: “As long as it’s not Scarlet, who cares?
who cares.usageNote: A common phrase. Good to understand.

your majesty.meaning: The words you say to a queen or a king.
your majesty.example: “We’ll find it, Your Majesty,” said the tallest guard.

by accident.example: What if her tail brushed someone’s wing by accident?

shut up.meaning: A rude order to stop talking.

come back.example: “The rest are still looking, but we wanted to come back and make sure you were guarded, in case it was a trick.

go ahead.example: “I’ll just go ahead and show her.

hold on.meaning: To grip something so you do not fall.

set on fire.example: Some of them really deserved to be set on fire.

good grief.meaning: Words you say when you are annoyed or surprised.
